said.t: Russia and Ukraine exchanged drone strikes Saturday, killing at least two people and injuring 20 others, officials on both sides said.
Russia’s Defense Ministry said its air defenses intercepted and destroyed 1,246 Ukrainian fixed-wing drones overnight.
Ukraine’s air force said Russia launched 162 attack drones, of which 141 were shot down or suppressed.

Russian forces carried out more than 20 drone attacks across four districts in Ukraine’s Dnipropetrovsk region, wounding five people, including a child, regional military administration chief Oleksandr Hanzha said on Telegram.
It said the targets included an electrical substation in Bila Tserkva, a fuel tank in Kiliya in the Odesa region and four locomotives in the Dnipropetrovsk, Zhytomyr and Kharkiv regions.
Russian forces have attacked Ukraine with 155 attack drones of various types and Parodiya decoy UAVs since the evening of 26 November.
A total of 110 drones have been destroyed, although some hits have been recorded.
Source: Ukraine's Air Force Quote: "As of 08:00, [Ukrainian] air defence forces had destroyed or jammed 110 Shahed (51 jet-powered), Gerbera and other types of drones.

According to the military, from 18:00 on Thursday, 26 November, Russian invaders deployed 155 Shahed-type strike drones (83 of which were jet-powered), ‘Herbera’ drones and ‘Parody’-type decoy drones to attack Ukraine.

Preliminary figures indicate that, as of 08:00 on Friday, air defences had shot down or jammed 110 Russian Shahed-type drones (51 of which were jet-powered), ‘Herbera’ drones and other types of drones.
Air strikes by the invaders were recorded at 27 locations, whilst the wreckage of downed targets was found at a further four.

The National Council of Canadian Muslims (NCCM), one of the groups that challenged Bill 21, called the ruling “a dark day in our constitutional democracy”.
Quebec used it when it passed Bill 21 in 2019 and renewed it in 2024.

26, that Russian President Vladimir Putin would be welcome at next month’s G20 summit in Florida, despite mounting bipartisan calls in Congress to withdraw his invitation.

Trump’s remarks came just days after 17 US lawmakers renewed bipartisan calls for the president to withdraw Putin’s invitation, citing Russia’s ongoing war against Ukraine and intelligence assistance to Iran.

19 letter led by Congressmen Pat Ryan, Gil Cisneros and Don Bacon, the lawmakers raised concerns over reports that Moscow had provided Tehran with satellite imagery and intelligence that may have assisted Iranian attacks on US forces.
23 statement , Ryan called Trump’s invitation to Putin “a betrayal of our troops,” warning that it would embolden Moscow in its war against Ukraine.
In September, a bipartisan group of 14 US senators, including Jeanne Shaheen, Mitch McConnell, Roger Wicker and Thom Tillis, urged Trump to withdraw Putin’s invitation.

Source: Trump speaking to journalists on Thanksgiving, as reported by European Pravda Details: Commenting on the possible attendance of Kremlin leader Vladimir Putin at the G20 leaders' summit in Florida in December, Trump recalled that Russia had been expelled from the G8 (now the G7).

Trump suggested that he might invite his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelenskyy to the G20 summit.
